paragraphs: Auve Tech develops and manufactures autonomous transportation systems. What it sells is more than the vehicle: the offer covers integration of the vehicles into a given environment and fleet management alongside them. The stated aim is to extend public transport with a weatherproof first and last mile link running from a bus, tram or train stop to the doorstep.

The current shuttle, MiCa, is electronically limited to 25 km/h. The specification lists operating time of up to twenty hours a day. Sensing hardware named on the product page includes lidar, radar, GNSS and an inertial measurement unit. Teleoperation and remote monitoring are offered as options. A later software version added dynamic reaction to objects, detection of overtaking vehicles and side detection.

The company traces its origin to a 2018 project run in cooperation with Tallinn University of Technology. Testing of the earlier Iseauto shuttle on Estonian public streets began in the summer of 2020. One case study describes a scheduled last mile service in Takamatsu, Japan, with the shuttle operated by Boldly. That route ran 2.6 kilometres between a car park and a viewpoint.

quote.text: MiCa, the successor to the well-received Iseauto, was launched in 2022.
